question: Does the trained 3-pass loop hold up as context grows, and is it a plausible long-context mechanism for the 35B?

q2.note: 2-bit expert mix; one 20 GB card, full GPU offload, f16 KV

q8.note: 8-bit; 32k requires CPU-offloaded experts on a 20 GB card, so the fair Q8 runs use the stable 16-layer offload configuration

fixed_target.method: Each slice ends at the same paragraph boundary. The 2048-token target at the end of the first n_ctx tokens is therefore identical across context lengths. Nominal C uses n_ctx = C + 1024 because the strided harness adds stride/2.

broad_ppl.note: These runs score different target spans and different numbers of 2k blocks. They are useful as a position/context survey, not as a clean context-length comparison; use fixed_target for that.

q8_offload20_exploratory.note: The initial overnight Q8 matrix used 20 CPU MoE layers. PPL is stable through 16 layers and jumps at 18; these numbers are not used for quant comparison. The loop ordering and needle outcomes from this run still matched Q2 and the fair Q8 reruns.

needles.method: Synthetic code 7391-ALPHA inserted at 10/50/90% of a wikitext-2 haystack; greedy, reasoning enabled, final-answer content scored. The 32k off-schedule runs were repeated with a 2048-token generation budget to rule out truncation.

sinks.verdict: A modest PPL cost at long context, but not required for retrieval. Secondary.

kv_precision.verdict: KV precision is not the mechanism.

controls.q8_offload_note: Stable through 17 layers, sharp break at 18. The fair Q8 32k runs use 16 layers; the initial 20-layer matrix is exploratory only.

findings: At a fixed 2k target, loop-3 PPL falls monotonically as context grows: Q2 7.107 -> 6.544 and Q8 6.879 -> 6.331 from 4k to 32k. The loop uses the longer context; it does not degrade.
Loop 3 is 1.6-1.8x better than loops 2 and 4 at every fixed-target context, and it is the only schedule that reliably emits a 32k needle answer (3/3 at all depths for both quants).
Loops 2 and 4 fail at 32k even with a 2048-token generation budget. They sometimes locate the code in reasoning but do not emit a final answer. The trained 3-pass schedule is essential, not cosmetic.
Q8 is slightly better than Q2 at every fixed-target context (6.33 vs 6.54 at 32k, ~3%). The loop survives 2-bit experts and benefits modestly from higher weight precision.
Attention sinks cost ~6-8% PPL at 8k/16k/32k but are not needed for 32k retrieval. They are secondary to the block bank and the loop message gates.
The earlier Q8 20-layer-offload PPL was an execution-path artifact: Q8 PPL is stable through 16-17 offloaded MoE layers and breaks at 18. The fair Q8 reruns use 16 layers.
caveats: One corpus (wikitext-2 test), one fixed target region, one 2k scored target. Absolute PPL is not comparable to the earlier wiki-blue corpus.
The needle is synthetic and the haystack is wiki prose; a harder long-document QA set is still needed.
Nominal 4k/8k/16k/32k use actual contexts 5.1k/9.2k/17.4k/33.8k because the strided harness adds 1024 tokens.
Q8 32k requires a CPU-offloaded expert configuration on the 20 GB card. The fair runs use the stable 16-layer configuration; this is a measurement configuration, not a deployment recommendation.
The 2048-token off-schedule rerun covered all Q2 depths and the Q8 50% depth; the Q8 10/90% off-schedule cases still used the shorter budget.
The loop-2/4 failure is a final-answer failure, not always a retrieval failure; reasoning sometimes contains the code.
The 16k slice tokenizes to 17,407 tokens before the boundary; the harness consumes one extra boundary token. The other three slices hit the exact count, and the same target text is used throughout.
what_it_means_for_35b: The loop is a plausible long-context fix: it improves prediction as context grows and preserves retrieval at 32k, unlike a shared-core-only or off-schedule loop.
The 35B loop must keep the block-attention bank and the trained 3-pass schedule. The 2k ablations already made the bank non-optional; the long-context data makes the depth schedule non-optional too.
The next long-context step is 64k/128k on Q2 if memory allows, plus a harder long-document QA set and a 35B-scale check.
